subject: Archaeology
title: Cuneiform: The First Writing System
description: A quick, practical guide to Cuneiform: The First Writing System.

hook.text: The oldest writing on earth was pressed into wet clay with a reed stylus. Over 500,000 tablets have survived.

buildup.text: Cuneiform started as pictures around 3400 BCE and evolved into abstract wedge-shaped marks representing sounds.

discovery.text: Henry Rawlinson deciphered cuneiform in the 1840s using a trilingual inscription carved high on a cliff at Behistun.

twist.text: Cuneiform was used by Sumerians, Akkadians, Babylonians, Assyrians, Hittites, and even Persians.

climax.text: AI is now being used to read damaged tablets. Machine learning can fill in broken signs that humans struggle to read.

punchline.text: They wrote on mud with a stick. Five hundred thousand of those notes survived.

quiz.question: How was cuneiform deciphered?
options: A bilingual dictionary was found in a sealed library in Babylon
Henry Rawlinson used a trilingual inscription carved on a cliff at Behistun
Scholars compared it to Egyptian hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone
